clue.text: Code word used in part of speech — Oscar

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about a part of speech, with a nod to Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'speech' and the start of 'Oscar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is the NATO phonetic alphabet's code word for the letter E.

clue.text: Hillbilly's endless criticism following game

indicators.note: following means the criticism piece comes after the game piece

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a ball game

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for criticism is cut off

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'

explanation.surface: A country type suffers non-stop carping after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union; 'stick' (as in 'getting stick') loses its K.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is an unsophisticated country dweller, the same stereotype as a hillbilly.

clue.text: Exhausted, exited to prolonged applause

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for worn out, done for
second meaning: a performer literally applauded off the stage

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: someone clapped all the way out of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is informal British slang for an old, worn-out machine or a tired person.

clue.text: Count made by Church of England over North and South America

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'over' puts the church letters on top of the rest

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
S is the compass abbreviation for south
US, the United States, stands for America

explanation.surface: The Anglican church extends its reach across both American continents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North and South America' looks like one place, but it is three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population.

clue.text: Recalled papers and periodical having go about one baseball legend

indicators.note: recalled, called back, turns the papers abbreviation round

parts.note: ID is identification papers
a mag is a magazine, a periodical

indicators.note: about means the go letters wrap around the numeral

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws documents and a magazine and has another try at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns only the papers, not the periodical as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe DiMaggio was a celebrated New York Yankees centre fielder, famous for his 56-game hitting streak.

clue.text: Piercing wail

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as sharp, cutting, as a ... wind
second meaning: to wail in mourning

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like one shrill cry; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means sharp as an adjective, and as a verb it means to lament loudly for the dead.

clue.text: Bid to run off with members

indicators.note: off, as in gone wrong, tells us the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: An offer to elope with some MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' looks like an attempt; it is a call in the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: No-trumps is a call in contract bridge naming a contract with no trump suit.

clue.text: Place of worship moving a celebrant

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the words that follow change places

explanation.surface: A priest's procession stirs the congregation in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a sanctuary or meeting house used for religious services.

clue.text: Cryptic clue about Republican devoid of pity

indicators.note: about means the scrambled word goes round the party letter
cryptic, obscure or puzzling, says the following word is scrambled

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint about a heartless Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clue' looks like a crossword phrase, but 'Cryptic' is the anagram signal: CLUE becomes CUEL, around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cruel is merciless, without compassion.

clue.text: Weird email describing the Parisian, unknown old novelist

indicators.note: describing here means drawing round, so the scrambled letters enclose the rest
weird, strange or odd, signals the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A strange email tells of a mysterious elderly French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was the French naturalist novelist who wrote Germinal and J'accuse.

clue.text: Love court work for powerful organisation

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A romance lawsuit becomes the work of a mighty institution.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is figuratively an organisation with far-reaching tentacles of influence.

clue.text: Racecourse that may provide a popular service for one

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
the service tree is a species of tree, so service is one example of a tree

explanation.surface: A racecourse whose catering offers a popular service.
explanation.walkthrough: The service tree is a European tree related to the rowan; 'for one' says it is an example of TREE. Aintree, near Liverpool, hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is the English racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run each year.

clue.text: Picked up money in store

indicators.note: picked up, as in heard over a line, signals a sound-alike

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Someone collects money that was kept in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a shop; it is a hidden hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden stockpile of supplies or valuables.

clue.text: Become angry — some poor golfers no doubt do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to turn aggressive or bad-tempered

definitions.text: some poor golfers no doubt do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bad golfer gouges turf out of the rough, the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the idiom literally: the rough is the long grass off the fairway, which wayward golfers hack at.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up rough is a British idiom for turning quarrelsome or violent.

clue.text: Noteworthy article describing male railway worker

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the first two pieces enclose the male letter

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable, striking, as in a signal achievement
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A remarkable article describes a man who works on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' as an adjective (a signal success) means noteworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A signalman operates the signals and points controlling train movements.

clue.text: Manage a day with head of government department

parts.note: a minister heads a government department

explanation.surface: Someone runs a day's business alongside a departmental chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' looks like a first-letter signal, but the whole phrase is the minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to run, direct or be in charge of affairs.

clue.text: Tunes do so much if adapted properly for film

indicators.note: adapted properly means the letters of the preceding words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Songs achieve a great deal when suitably adapted for the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first stretch, 'Tunes do so much if', is the fodder; the surface reads like a comment on film scores.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1965 Rodgers and Hammerstein musical starring Julie Andrews is a famous movie.

clue.text: A German beer mug for eminent scientist

parts.note: ein is German for 'a'
a stein is a large earthenware beer mug

explanation.surface: A German raises a beer mug to toast a great scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist behind relativity, is the archetypal great scientist.

clue.text: Novitiate, one they ordered to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged letters hold the quiet letter inside
ordered, put in a new order, tells us the two words are rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A trainee monk is told to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command to the novice; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a novice or beginner, especially a newly admitted member of a religious order.

clue.text: A red iron pot in ground

indicators.note: ground, as in crushed or milled, says the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something red is crushed in an iron cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil or crushed spice; it is the anagram signal for IRON POT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a grape variety and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: Meal about finished

parts.note: re means about, concerning
past means over, finished

explanation.surface: A meal is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About finished' reads as 'almost over', but 'about' is RE, the word used in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: Glass initially embedded in bare elbow

indicators.note: embedded in puts the picked letter inside the word for bare

parts.note: nude means bare, unclothed

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word before

parts.note: first letter of glass

explanation.surface: A shard of glass gets stuck in someone's bare elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elbow' looks like the body part; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to nudge or jostle them with the arm.

clue.text: Golf club's chauffeur

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the club used for long tee shots
second meaning: a person employed to drive

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a club's own chauffeur; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Driver names both the long-hitting golf wood and someone who drives a car for an employer.

clue.text: Wealthiest heading off to find flightless bird?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: wealthiest is most rich

explanation.surface: The richest people set off to look for a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 'wealthiest' as MOST RICH and drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the large African bird that runs but cannot fly.

clue.text: Uncertain moment heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A doubtful moment as someone sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or of questionable quality.

clue.text: Pressing part of leg nipped by boxer

indicators.note: nipped by means held inside the boxer word

parts.note: pug is slang for a pugilist, a boxer
the shin is the front of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A boxer bites a fighter's leg in a heated moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests the dog, which fits 'nipped'; it is the fighter, PUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing means urging insistently, the same as pressing.

clue.text: Artist, Hockney, ultimately shown in Indian state

indicators.note: shown in means the letter is placed inside the state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of the name

parts.note: last letter of Hockney

explanation.surface: An exhibition of David Hockney's work is held in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Hockney looks like the artist of the definition, but only his last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the Spanish painter of The Third of May 1808.

clue.text: Good runs seen before if following this extraordinary snooker champion

indicators.note: seen before means the first two letters come ahead of the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: extraordinary means the letters of the next word are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Plenty of runs come before this remarkable champion takes the table.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS rearranged gives ITHS. Terry Griffiths won the World Snooker Championship in 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Griffiths, the Welsh player, was the 1979 world snooker champion.

clue.text: Hostile force some cavalrymen eventually repelled

indicators.note: repelled, driven back, means the run of letters is read backwards
some means only part of these words is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An opposing army is driven back by a cavalry charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The run YMENE spans 'cavalrymen eventually' and reads backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the opposing army in a war, a hostile military force.
